data.name: Title
data.value: Picture modes

data.name: Intro
data.value: Click a mode: brightness, blue light, tone curve and color vibrance are set together. It does not touch the refresh rate, the calibration or the monitor's color preset.

data.name: Recommended
data.value: recommended

data.name: BestTitle
data.value: For the best picture (once)

data.name: BestStep1
data.value: 1. Monitor settings tab: Color preset Neutral (6500K, the most accurate built-in one); Custom RGB if you will run the setup wizard. Sharpness 4 (factory).

data.name: BestStep2
data.value: 2. Setup wizard: matches the white to the Pixel's screen and sets gamma 2.2 and grey balance by eye with patterns. This gives the most accurate color.

data.name: BestStep3
data.value: 3. Day for everyday work; Cinema modes for movies (by room light); Long use modes for hours of work.

data.name: Purpose_Day
data.value: The most accurate picture for daytime and everyday work: no effects, 6500K white.

data.name: Purpose_Evening
data.value: Evening, the hours before sleep: clear blue light reduction (3400K). For long reading Comfort · Evening is less tiring.

data.name: Purpose_Night
data.value: Short use right before bed: least blue light (2700K) and low brightness.

data.name: Purpose_Code
data.value: Long reading and code: slightly warm white (5000K); white pages don't glare.

data.name: Purpose_Film
data.value: Movies and series in a bright room: vivid colors (offsets the TN panel's washed-out look), standard tone. Not accurate color, pleasing color.

data.name: Purpose_Game
data.value: Games: a little brighter and more vivid colors.

data.name: Purpose_DaVinci
data.value: DaVinci timeline: neutral, no effects; color decisions are made on the phone.

data.name: Purpose_Cinema
data.value: Movies in a dim room (a lamp on): gamma 2.4, the value films are mastered for, gives deep midtones while shadows are kept; 6500K white, a little vibrance.

data.name: Purpose_CinemaDark
data.value: Movies with the lights off: low brightness doesn't glare and deepens the TN panel's grey black; gamma 2.4; a little more vibrance because colors look paler in the dark. A soft 6500K light behind the monitor (bias light) makes black look deeper.

data.name: Purpose_CinemaVivid
data.value: Animation, action, documentaries: vivid contrast curve and strong vibrance; a fuller, punchier picture. Not accurate color.

data.name: Purpose_CinemaNight
data.value: A movie before bed: low brightness and mild warm white (4500K) affect sleep less; gamma 2.4 stays.

data.name: Purpose_ComfortDay
data.value: Hours of work in daylight: brightness suited to the room, slightly warm white (5500K), no effects.

data.name: Purpose_ComfortEvening
data.value: Long reading and work in a dim room: lower brightness, mild warm white (4500K: the least tiring range in research), no effects.

data.name: Purpose_ComfortNight
data.value: Long use in a dark room: lowest backlight (no extra dimming), 4000K. Very warm white (2700K) tires more in long reading.

data.name: GroupHint_Cinema
data.value: 24 fps movies judder at 60 Hz; at 72 Hz every frame is shown for the same time (add 72 Hz in NVIDIA first: Guide, section 2). Modes don't touch the refresh rate.

data.name: GroupHint_Comfort
data.value: What tires the eyes most is a screen much brighter than the room: a white page should not look brighter than the wall next to it. Every 20 minutes look 6 m away for 20 seconds (20-20-20).
